# Exact-head refresh campaign, 2026-09-08

## Causal improvement campaign

The `perf/pr-improve-20260908` successor keeps the same pinned main and acceptance tolerances. New source fixes receive new exact candidate pins. Shared microbenchmarks now capture CLR MethodJittingStarted events alongside runtime boundary samples to identify residual compilation activity; this instrumentation applies identically to A1/B/A2. Its observer cost remains in the measured process. No compilation event or latency sample is excluded, and these diagnostic runs cannot substitute for missing loaded acceptance evidence. Compare each result with the preceding exact-head refresh and preserve both.

The outbox suite retains its preceding four-case fixture, twenty-second direct warmup, thirty BDN warmups, twenty-five measured samples, tiered compilation disabled, and stricter 1% timing/2% control drift limits. It adds the same JIT attribution logger. All listener modes remain measured, including the enabled baseline's known lack of instruments. Duration tracking moved outside the disabled product path; that causal candidate requires fresh measurement of enabled and disabled modes.

The dispatch refresh runner exposed two physical cores with two hardware threads each. Fixed logical CPU numbers did not ensure physical isolation between the consumer and upstream processes. The next experiment reads Linux CPU/core/socket topology, gives the consumer every available hardware thread of the last physical core, and confines the baseline producer and Kafka to the other core(s). It rejects machines exposing fewer than two physical cores and records the complete mapping. Workloads, rates, durations, runtime settings, raw latency retention and acceptance tolerances remain unchanged. This addresses resource interference; it does not waive latency losses, startup transitions or missing loaded shutdown coverage.

Subsequent shared microbenchmark runs isolate every declared case in a fresh process, preventing preceding cases from changing process-wide pools and runtime state. Both full matrices validate before timing; each isolated selection must return exactly its declared case and 25 samples. A1/B/A2 order, fixtures, per-case warmup, affinity, JIT settings and tolerances remain unchanged. The #3086 response-pool negative-control discrepancy and #3116 cross-case runtime activity motivate this revision; prior results remain retained.

Administrative probes retain their complete-entry primer, 180-second warmup, 60-second measurement, configuration matrix and original tolerances. Each fresh single-concurrency process now has fixed affinity to the last allowed logical CPU and records CLR compilation names with monotonic phase markers. This tests migration/runtime-state explanations for unchanged common-method drift; it does not assume the previous adverse observations were harmless. All observer allocations, CPU, GC and latency samples remain included. Existing broker integration CI remains correctness evidence; this cached-transport diagnostic does not claim measured broker performance or automatic acceptance.

The pool-loaded suite extends the existing interval/block-histogram fixture from `perf/pr-3142-loaded-evidence`. It measures 1,000-byte/three-partition and 65,536-byte/one-partition closed-loop producer-consumer completion. Warmup is now uniformly 180 seconds and measurement 300 seconds in each fresh process; this supersedes the old fixture's prospective 60-second warmup. Both products build and both configurations validate with 12/13-second smoke phases before any acceptance-length measurements. A1/B/A2 run sequentially on one Ubuntu VM with fresh brokers per configuration and physical-core client/broker separation. The fixture preserves all-message delivery/completion p50/p99/max, CPU and allocations per completed message, one-second extrema, ten-second distributions, runtime/GC/heap/RSS/backlog observations, and default shutdown outcomes. Docker broker resource observations remain separate. CLR compilation attribution is identical across phases. The prior 3% adverse/control limits remain; collection validation alone cannot PASS. Cold reset-failure performance, loaded failure/shutdown-under-ingress and maximum uncertainty remain explicit review requirements. Reservoir 1.7.0 comparisons permit only their intentional dependency change. Pool MemoryDiagnoser also gains JIT attribution, with its normal workload/settings unchanged.

Candidate SHAs are explicit workflow inputs and must contain the baseline. Preserve each PR's prior evidence; new pins supersede old-head acceptance, not historical observations.

Pool rent/return uses the unchanged fixture from `perf/pool-reset-count-3141`, with explicit product inputs. Both products run the same fixture, twenty elapsed seconds of direct workload, thirty one-second BDN warmups, twenty-five actual iterations, and tiered compilation/PGO enabled. Predeclare microbenchmark mean-time loss tolerance 3% against each control, maximum control drift 5%, and no candidate per-message allocation increase. Require 0 B on per-message hot paths; distinguish per-batch and cold-path allocation. Report absolute A1/B/A2, both deltas, control drift, sample counts and confidence bounds. No script turns workflow success into a performance PASS.

Administrative direct-call probes reuse the existing PR-specific fixture and accounting validators. The dispatch fixture from `pr-3117-hosted-evidence` now initializes and verifies zero committed offsets before any warmup or producer offers. Run 34218648542 completed all 12,050,000 baseline records but failed its first offset commit with NotCoordinator as the broker initialized __consumer_offsets at shutdown. Setup retries only retriable Kafka errors, at most five attempts; a failed preflight still aborts. No measured error is caught or suppressed. Final commit/drain assertions, all loads, warmup durations, timing boundaries and tolerances stay unchanged. The failed run is preserved and never treated as a candidate regression or complete A1/B/A2. The correction applies identically to every baseline, candidate and smoke process.
# Broker sampler correction

The first loaded pool collection stopped after a successful baseline smoke because the Docker stats stream ignored termination. Use bounded `docker stats --no-stream` observations, with a 10-second command timeout and a one-second delay between observations. Preserve the last sample and propagate sampling errors. This fixes collection shutdown; workload settings and acceptance requirements remain unchanged. No measured A1/B/A2 phase ran in the failed attempts.
# Share parser reaper warmup and header coverage

Run 34238063366 isolates each case but captures the first `RunIdleConnectionReaperAsync` continuation and `ReapIdleConnectionsAsync` JIT about five seconds into measurement. ConnectionPool caps its timer interval at 60 seconds; the prior 50-second workload warmup misses this periodic path. For #3116, predeclare 130 one-second workload warmup iterations and require at least 120 measured seconds of workload warmup in every fresh process. Keep the reaper enabled and retain all samples. Keep 25 actual iterations and the existing tolerances. Add the existing 64-record/two-header configuration to the 1024-record/no-header configuration, covering all seven methods in both configurations. Both matrices must match and validate before A1. Full acceptance still requires runtime, CPU/latency/stability and recovery review.
# Loaded pool broker retention

Run 34240997161 exhausted the runner disk during A1: its baseline warmup alone completed 58,310,646 1,000-byte messages. Unlimited broker retention invalidates this sustained closed-loop experiment. Cancel the matching #3142 attempt and preserve both attempts. Before any replacement run, configure broker retention to 1 GiB per partition, 16 MiB segments, a one-second retention check and a one-second segment deletion delay. This greatly exceeds the 1,024-slot in-flight bound (64 MiB at the largest message size); completed-message/offset/slot assertions still reject loss or skipped work. All A1/B/A2 phases use these exact settings and retain broker stats plus runner disk-free samples. Smoke phases must validate before timing. No result from the full-disk experiment qualifies for acceptance.
# Binary-key concurrency coverage

The next #3082 candidate bypasses key hashing and lane queues only when both maximum batch size and handler concurrency are one: partition FIFO already preserves key order. Keep the original concurrency-one workloads and add concurrency four to every repeated-key, string-control and distinct-key case (18 cases total). This exposes the remaining full-content hashing cost in the concurrent path rather than allowing the sequential specialization to hide it. All phases use identical fixtures, 50 one-second warmup iterations, 25 actual iterations and unchanged acceptance tolerances. Empty/null/collision behavior remains covered by product tests.
# Follower-retry normal-path loaded comparison

The isolated #3086 micro comparison (34238059150) removes the response-pool control discrepancy: all eight means meet the existing point limits, with no measured-iteration JIT growth. Run the same retained pool-loaded fixture against #3086 to assess normal successful producer/consumer completion on a real Kafka broker. Keep its two message/partition configurations, 180-second warmup, 300-second measurements, retention settings and 3% protected-metric/control-drift limits. CPU and allocations cover the combined producer/consumer client process; broker resources remain separate. This complements the error-response fixture and correctness tests. It does not simulate follower recovery, relabel the baseline's incorrect reset behavior, or imply acceptance before uncertainty/startup/stability review.
